title: The hidden logic of emotion.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: There are no data files to open. Europe PMC's record for this DOI reports isOpenAccess=N, inEPMC=N, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, hasDbCrossReferences=N, hasTMAccessionNumbers=N, and no PMCID, so no full text, no supplementary file list and no accession numbers exist. The NCBI PubMed summary (PMID 42424444) shows Science volume 393, issue 6807, pages 145-146 - a two-page item by Xiaowei Gu and Joshua P. Johansen with a single-sentence abstract, i.e. a Perspective-style commentary. A web search returned only the PubMed entry and news aggregators, no repository deposit.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The one-sentence abstract: 'Internal emotion models unify research across species and spark fresh ideas for treating anxiety and trauma.' The body text is paywalled and was not retrieved; per project rules I did not scrape the publisher site.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. This is a two-page opinion/Perspective piece (Science 393:145-146), not a research or resource paper. It has no supplementary files, no data availability statement, no database accessions and no repository deposit. There is nothing to download, so the evaluation stops here.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use brain activity recordings to predict an animal's internal emotional state across different species and situations.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would need recorded neural activity (for example electrode or imaging traces from amygdala and related regions) paired with behaviour, for many trials across several animals. This commentary supplies none of it; the number of examples available is zero.
plain_idea.predict: An emotion-like internal state label (for example threat versus safety, or a graded fear level) whose ground truth would come from measured behavioural readouts such as freezing, escape, or heart rate during a controlled conditioning experiment.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups studying fear and anxiety circuits would gain a way to compare internal states across species and labs, which is the explicit goal the commentary argues for. But that project needs the primary recordings from the research papers this piece discusses, not this piece.

ml_idea: None available from this article. If the underlying topic is of interest, go directly to the primary research papers on internal emotion states that this Perspective comments on (Gu and Johansen discuss cross-species emotion-state work), and evaluate those for deposited electrophysiology or behaviour data instead.

effort.compute_note: No compute estimate is meaningful because no data exists to process.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check Europe PMC's hasData/hasSuppl flags and the page range. Pages 145-146 with a one-sentence abstract identifies a Perspective, which never carries data - this took one API call.

verdict_reason: This is a two-page Science Perspective (a commentary on other people's research), not a research or resource paper. It has no supplementary files, no accessions, no data availability statement and no repository deposit, so Part A1 fails outright and there is nothing to model.
